chapter: Young players, schools and studio work
title: Schools should teach scales and chords
summary: Maxwell tells pupils to learn scales and chords in self-defence and says schools should point out older players' value.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

listen to them.
You speak of them going to school. I feel, then, it's the school's fault. The school should not -- that's the point of a school, the older people are trying to help the younger. They're not trying to stand up there and say, I want to learn this and the teacher say, okay, I'll teach you. Do you want to be a thorough musician? Then this is what you do and don't tell me what to do, or you don't need to come to this school.

Which is what I tell my pupils, you know. If you know so damn well what you should do on a trumpet, what are you coming to me for? If you want me to make you a good player, then you leave that up to me and don't tell me what to give you. Not because of my angle, but because I want to be honest wil you, I can't teach you if I do what you want to do. They say, I don't want to learn the scales, I don't want to learn the chords, man, I want to play out, I want to play space that?" "Oh, you don't have to music. I say "what is / follow the chords or the scales or anything. I say, well, you ought to learn the scales and chords because someday you might learn one by mistake and everybody will put you down, you know. If you don't know what they are, you might play one by mistake.
So you ought to learn one in self-defense. I figure I'll get around it that way. So the responsibility is not
entirely the younger players, because the reason they go to school is to learn. The people there should not be afraid to point out the value of these older players.
